sentences.span: 10yr US real yields rising +9.8bps to a post-2008 high of 2.87% but 10yr breakevens actually falling by -1.3bps
sentences.why: Exact match on both figures and direction; 'inflation rate priced into the bond market' is a faithful plain-English rendering of breakevens.

sentences.span: The former has now risen +97bps in 2026 and the latter only +9bps... term premium have been range bound for around 18 months so the sell-off isn't really fiscal related
sentences.why: 97bp/9bp figures match exactly; 'term premium' = 'extra yield for holding long maturities' and 'not fiscal related' = 'argues against a deficit story' are faithful glosses, not distortions.

sentences.span: accepted just $4.078 billion, which is only 68% of the $6 billion cap... yields spiked to a new multi-decade high
sentences.why: Every figure and the causal yield-spike claim match directly.

sentences.span: if you want to carry significant length in stocks, marry it with a trading short in bonds (GS Pasquariello) / policymaker panic to cap yields has begun, time to nibble bonds (BofA Hartnett)
sentences.why: Goldman and BofA take genuinely opposite bond-direction calls in the same window; transition sentence names no unsupported figures.

sentences.span: policymaker panic to cap yields has begun, time to nibble bonds...returns = 10% in 5-year, 14% in 10-year, 22% in 30-year UST should yields drop 100bps next 12 months
sentences.why: All figures match and the conditional ('if yields fall') is correctly preserved as conditional, not asserted.

sentences.span: We expect the Fed to hike in October and December, with a hold thereafter, but the market is pricing almost four additional hikes from here.
sentences.why: Exact verbatim match of attribution, direction, and figures.

sentences.span: If we only look at times when we had this reading and weren't coming out of a bear market, it was late '99 early '00.
sentences.why: BTIG's since-1990 breadth screen isolates exactly one non-bear-market prior occurrence, Dec 1999-Jan 2000, matching the sentence.

sentences.span: It's now been 213 trading days since the last 80%+ NYSE downside volume day. The average calendar year sees 21 such days
our equity analysts estimate that the hyperscalers need to generate annual AI revenues of roughly $300 billion in the next few years to break even on their investments
sentences.why: Figure and 'breakeven' framing match exactly, correctly distinguished from other figures in the same note.

sentences.span: What would make us BEARISH: ...would likely be initiated by a capex cut.
sentences.why: Attribution (JPMorgan trading desk) and the capex-cut-as-bearish-signal claim match directly.

sentences.span: the contract Oracle is still liable to pay a "carry cost" in lieu of rent payments for up to three years... a fee that would cover the interest payments to debt holders in full as well as a certain level of equity return... "The power delivery risk sits with Oracle, not the investors"
sentences.why: Every clause matches: carry cost in lieu of rent (3 years), lenders' interest plus equity return, power delivery risk on the tenant.

sentences.span: unveiling Muse (META stock up 45% in 25 trading days on the news!!) / Note, GSXUSWCH has declined -12% since launch in end August.
sentences.why: 45%/25-trading-days figure matches; GSXUSWCH ('Consumer Inertia' basket, i.e. companies dependent on customers not switching) down 12% since end-August launch matches exactly.

sentences.span: Within six months, Amazon, Google, Microsoft, and Apple will all ship their own versions... a race to the bottom where the winner is the one who can burn the most cash the longest... We love a META put spread here for a trade.
sentences.why: Named platforms (four), six-month timeline, cash-burn framing, and put-spread call all match directly.

sentences.span: BofA, for its part, has flagged diesel as the key real-economy pressure point, warning that prices near these levels have historically echoed inflation spikes above 5%
sentences.why: Attribution, framing (diesel vs headline crude), and the 5% figure all match directly.

sentences.span: Per Goldman, an estimated "64% of S&P 500 Index corporates had entered the blackout window as of 09/21/26,"... Rising to ~85% by week-end means the corporate bid steps back just as CTAs are set up to sell.
sentences.why: 64% as of 9/21 and ~85% by week-end match exactly; 'largest price-insensitive bid' and CTAs-as-trend-followers-positioned-to-sell both match the source's own framing.
